title: The Moon height map is the right way round
criterion: Known craters are low, Mons Malapert is high, and only one orientation of the map fits
summary: There are 8 possible ways to orient the map. 1 of them puts all 7 known craters and mountains in the right place: the one that the app uses. With the first threshold (1.0 km for craters), 0 of 8 fitted. The report gives the history.

title: Our Sun and Earth directions agree with NASA JPL Horizons
criterion: Sun within 0.001 degrees and Earth within 0.01 degrees, at 8 places and 300 times each, from the file that the app uses
summary: The largest difference at 8 places and 300 times: Sun 0.000192 degrees, Earth 0.005983 degrees. At times on the 10-minute grid the largest difference is 0.005980 degrees. At times halfway between two grid points it is 0.005983 degrees.

title: The horizon calculation is correct on test shapes
criterion: Agreement with exact formulas, correct compass direction, correct result after a rotation and after halving the step
summary: 14 of 14 automated tests passed. They cover 4 requirements.

title: Sunlight at 3 places compared with NASA's published light map
criterion: The difference at each place is reported. An exact match is not expected: the time span, the map detail and the observer height differ
summary: At 3 places, our share of time with the Sun in view is at most 6.1 percentage points away from the NASA values around the place (allowed: 15). Shackleton rim (high point): ours 88%, NASA 0 to 85%; Haworth rim (high point): ours 41%, NASA 24 to 39%; Mons Malapert (summit): ours 67%, NASA 49 to 60%.

title: Countdowns and totals are correct
criterion: Agreement with a slow, simple count for the time to sunset and Earthset and for the totals of a stay
summary: 17 of 17 automated tests passed. They cover 5 requirements.
